dedupe_keys.name: agrobench multimodal benchmark for weakly supervised crop yield learning 2026

description: AgroBench is a benchmark that turns public US county crop yield statistics into weakly supervised pixel-level crop time series for machine learning. Each crop pixel's time series is paired with its county's reported yield as a weak label, not a measured pixel yield. Its pipeline combines USDA yield statistics with crop-specific land cover masks, Sentinel-2 multispectral imagery, Sentinel-1 radar, climate variables and terrain data into aligned sequences over the growing season. It was produced by Udaiveer Singh, Rajiv Ranjan, Shashank Tamaskar and Dharmendra Saraswat and described in an arXiv preprint submitted on 16 September 2026. Coverage is the United States: over 13 million observations from 788,654 crop pixels in 5,107 county-year combinations for five major crops, across the eight seasons 2017 to 2024. Licence (read on 2026-09-29): CC-BY-4.0 (Zenodo archive and paper). Caveats: labels are county averages, so within-county variation is not observed, and it is a new preprint without peer review. For simulation it provides a standard Leave-One-Year-Out test for yield models, with baseline results, useful for building crop models that estimate how drought or heat years affect harvests. It is related to the USDA Cropland Data Layer record in this catalogue, a likely source of its crop masks.
